name: AspectRatio
summary: Keeps a box, and the image, video or embed inside it, at a fixed ratio of width to height at any width.
useWhen: A cover image, thumbnail or video that must not jump in height while it loads
An embed (a map or a video player) that should scale with its column
A grid of thumbnails that all share one ratio
avoidWhen: A single img or video you can style yourself: the native aspect-ratio CSS property on the element is simpler
Text content that must grow with its copy
An icon or avatar with a fixed size

ratio.description: Width divided by height, for example 16 / 9, 4 / 3, 1 or 3 / 4. A value that is not a positive finite number falls back to 16 / 9.

fit.description: How an img, video, iframe, picture or canvas child fills the box: cover crops, contain letterboxes. Sets data-fit. An inline svg fits through its own preserveAspectRatio.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element as the root through Radix Slot.

children.description: One media element, or any content that fills the box.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div. The media inside carries the name (alt text on img, a title track or label on video).
notes: The ratio box reserves its height before media loads, so the page does not shift.
Content taller than the box is clipped. Never put text a person needs inside a ratio box.

en.alt: Alt text on the media says what it shows, in sentence case. Decorative media gets an empty alt.

ar.alt: Alt text in Arabic for Arabic pages, no diacritics.

react.note: Radix renders a wrapper div (data-radix-aspect-ratio-wrapper) around the root that takes 100% width; className, style and ref go to the inner root. No motion: nothing animates.

angular.behavior: [dsAspectRatio] directive on the native aspect-ratio property
angular.note: No Radix in Angular: the host sets aspect-ratio from the ratio input, so there is no wrapper div. The shared CSS styles the root and its media the same way.

native.note: React Native has aspectRatio on every view; fit maps to Image resizeMode cover or contain.

styles.liquid: Layout only. Media stays solid under glass bars.

mistakes.wrong: An AspectRatio around one img that you style yourself
mistakes.right: aspect-ratio 16 / 9 on the img in your CSS, with object-fit cover

mistakes.wrong: A fixed height on a thumbnail so the grid lines up
mistakes.right: AspectRatio ratio 1 in each cell, which scales with the column

mistakes.wrong: A caption inside the ratio box
mistakes.right: The caption below the box, where it can wrap

mistakes.wrong: An AspectRatio placed straight in a grid or flex row that stretches its items
mistakes.right: Wrap it in a cell with align-self start, or set align start on the Grid or Stack: the Radix wrapper is the item, and a stretched wrapper loses the ratio

name: Bidi
summary: Isolates each Latin run inside Arabic copy, so sentence punctuation stays at the logical end of the line.
useWhen: Arabic copy with a Latin term in it: a product name, a file name, a format such as JSON, a URL
A sentence that ends right after a Latin word and shows its period on the wrong side
avoidWhen: English copy: it comes back unchanged, so the wrapper adds nothing
Copy with markup inside: Bidi takes plain text only
A whole paragraph in another language: give its element a lang attribute

insteadUse.A paragraph in English inside an Arabic: an element with lang en, or a Theme with lang en to change direction too

a11y.focus: Never focusable. It adds no role.
notes: Each run is a bdi element with dir ltr. A run that opens with neutrals, like ~/.cursor, gets an explicit direction instead of a guess.
No invisible marks (RLM, LRM, U+202A to U+202E) are typed into strings: the markup sets the direction.

react.note: Lives in packages/react/src/theme/Bidi.tsx. The splitting is splitLatinRuns in @the-system/shared.

angular.note: A pipe or a component on splitLatinRuns from @the-system/shared.

native.note: Text runs with writingDirection from splitLatinRuns.

mistakes.wrong: Typing an LRM mark after a Latin word in an Arabic string
mistakes.right: <Bidi>{text}</Bidi>, which wraps the run in bdi

mistakes.wrong: Wrapping the period in the isolate with the Latin word
mistakes.right: Let Bidi find the run: it never takes trailing punctuation

name: Button
summary: An action the person takes on this page: save, send, open, delete. The one control that renders a native button.
useWhen: An action that changes data or starts a task on this page
The main action of a form, a dialog or a card, as tone accent with emphasis solid
A secondary or quiet action next to the main one, as soft, outline or ghost
A link that must look like an action, through asChild
avoidWhen: A control with only an icon and no visible label
Navigation inside running text
A choice that stays on or off
More than one solid accent button in the same view

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px in the default density.

tone.description: The color family. accent is the primary action color of the active style.

emphasis.description: soft is the standard button of Studio and Desk (the source secondary). tone accent with emphasis solid is the primary action.

shape.description: default takes radius.control (Desk draws it as a pill), pill is fully round, square takes radius.sm.

loading.description: Shows the spinner and a visually hidden status (loadingLabel), sets aria-busy and data-loading, keeps the width and focus, blocks activation.

loadingLabel.description: What the hidden status says while loading, for example Saving changes or جار الحفظ.

disabled.description: Sets aria-disabled and data-disabled. Stays focusable so a Tooltip can say why. The native disabled attribute is never set. On an asChild link the href is removed while disabled.

start.description: Leading content: a system icon name or a node, before the label. Icons are 16px at every size, lg included, as in both sources.

end.description: Trailing content: a system icon name or a node, after the label. 16px at every size.

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of its container. Sets data-full-width.

wrap.description: Lets a long label wrap and the button grow in height. Off by default: the label ends in an ellipsis and the button shrinks with its row, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px. Sets data-wrap. Desk draws no roll on a wrapping label.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example a link, as the button.

type.description: Native type, so a button never submits a form by accident. Ignored with asChild.

a11y.role: button (native button element), or the role of the asChild element
a11y.focus: In the tab order in every state, disabled and loading included. A 2px ring on keyboard focus; every solid fill gets the doubled ring (focus.shadow.primary) so it reads against the fill.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label is the accessible name. While loading, a visually hidden status inside the button says loadingLabel (Loading by default) and aria-busy is set.
notes: Disabled and loading use aria-disabled, not the native disabled attribute, so focus never drops to the page when an action starts.

While disabled or loading, a click or middle click does not submit a form or follow an asChild link, and onClick, onAuxClick, onPointerDown and onKeyDown do not run. A disabled asChild link loses its href and keeps role link.
Icons inside the button are hidden from assistive tech. The label names the button.
Under forced colors the focus outline uses Highlight and the Desk roll is off.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip (wave 1).

en.label: A verb plus a noun in sentence case: Save changes, Delete project. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes.
en.busy: Keep the label while loading. Say the verb in progress (Saving changes) in a live region, not on the button.
en.danger: Name what goes: Delete project, not Delete.

ar.label: Noun form labels, no diacritics: حفظ التغييرات، حذف المشروع. Never the imperative.

react.note: Motion: press, named from the pattern catalog that arrives in wave 1. Today: instant color swaps, the spinner, and the Desk roll label.

angular.note: The host element is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; start and end take an icon name or a TemplateRef. No asChild: a[dsButton] is the link form, and an inert link loses its href. Disabled and loading block click and auxclick with a capture listener. Button.css is used as is.

native.note: Styles from createButtonStyles(theme, variants) on the generated theme objects; Desk pill through packages/styles/desk/native/Button.ts. hitSlop reaches 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android at every size. Press feedback: a Reanimated spring scale from spring.press, off under reduce motion. The Desk roll label is a web hover effect with no touch equivalent: not on native. No asChild and no token focus ring yet (the platform draws keyboard focus).

styles.studio: Bordered and filled overlay pills. The primary action is the neutral fill from color.primary (overlay 20 with the control border); the accent tint is the overlay too. Hover and press step the overlay at once.
styles.desk: Pill shaped at every size. The primary action is yellow #ffd84d with ink text and a doubled focus ring; accent soft is a yellow tint. The label rolls up on hover and keyboard focus, a copy rolling in from below (recipes/Button.css), off under reduced motion and forced colors and on a wrapping label.
styles.neutral: Planned: filled primary, outline secondary, 36 to 40px.
styles.liquid: Planned: capsule buttons with a press scale.

mistakes.wrong: Two solid accent buttons side by side
mistakes.right: One solid accent button for the main action, soft or ghost for the rest

mistakes.wrong: A button labelled OK or Continue
mistakes.right: A verb plus a noun that names the result: Save changes

mistakes.wrong: Swapping the label to Saving while loading
mistakes.right: loading on the button and the busy verb in a live region; the width holds

mistakes.wrong: A disabled button with no reason
mistakes.right: Leave it out, or keep it focusable and explain with a Tooltip

mistakes.wrong: An anchor styled with button classes
mistakes.right: Button with asChild around the anchor

mistakes.wrong: A Button with an icon and no visible text
mistakes.right: IconButton with a label

name: Container
summary: Centers page content at a max width with a gutter on both inline sides.
useWhen: The content column of a page or a landing section, centered on wide screens
Capping the line length of reading text at a narrow width
Keeping the 16px phone gutter on any page content
avoidWhen: Inside a panel, card or dialog that already has its own padding
Laying out children in a row or columns
A full bleed band of color or media that must reach the screen edges

width.description: The max inline size, gutter included: sm 30rem (breakpoint.phone), md 48rem (breakpoint.tablet), lg 68.75rem (breakpoint.desktop), xl desktop plus half a phone (about 86rem), full no cap. Named width, not size, because size is the shared control axis. Sets data-width.

gutter.description: Padding on both inline sides, a space.* step. 3xl is 16px on phones in the default density. Sets data-gutter.

as.description: The element to render. One main per page.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div, or the landmark of as
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Container is layout only.
notes: Content never scrolls sideways at 320px: the width is a max, the box is 100% and the gutter sits inside it (WCAG 1.4.10).
Width sm keeps reading text near 70 characters a line.

ar.body: No copy of its own. The gutter is the same on both sides, so nothing changes in Arabic.

react.note: No motion: a static layout has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies.

angular.note: The host element is the root, so as is not needed.

native.behavior: react-native:View with maxWidth, alignSelf center and paddingHorizontal
native.note: Respect the safe area insets on top of the gutter.

styles.desk: Layout only. Pages sit inside windows, so a Container is mostly for site pages.
styles.liquid: Layout only. Content scrolls under the glass bars; the gutter stays.

mistakes.wrong: A Container inside a Dialog body or a Card
mistakes.right: No Container: the panel already pads its content

mistakes.wrong: max-width 1200px and padding 0 16px written by hand
mistakes.right: Container width lg, which keeps the gutter and the logical margins

mistakes.wrong: size xl to pick a page width
mistakes.right: width xl; size is the control size axis

mistakes.wrong: Two Containers rendered as main on one page
mistakes.right: One main per page; the rest as div or section

name: Dialog
summary: A modal task that must be finished or dismissed. The page behind it is covered by a backdrop, hidden from assistive tech and out of reach until the dialog closes.
useWhen: A decision blocks the rest of the page
A short form of up to five fields
A destructive action that needs one more look before it runs
avoidWhen: Long content, or content compared with the page
A message that needs no decision
Work the person does next to the page, moving between both
An action that cannot be undone and must not be dismissed by accident

onOpenChange.description: Called with false for Escape, a backdrop click, the close control and DialogClose.

size.description: The width from the dialog.width tokens: 360, 440, 520, 640 and 820 px, never wider than the viewport minus a gutter.

tone.description: danger: a destructive decision. The title takes the danger color and focus opens on the Cancel action.

dismissible.description: false: only the dialog's own actions close it. Escape and a backdrop click do nothing and the close control is disabled (aria-disabled). For short waits while an action runs: the app sets it back to true when the action ends.

title.description: DialogContent: the title for the common case, the same as a DialogTitle as its first child.

description.description: DialogContent: the description for the common case.

closeLabel.description: DialogContent: the accessible name of the close control. Arabic default under lang ar: إغلاق النافذة.

controlsLabel.description: DialogContent: the accessible name of the Desk lights group.

rootProps.description: DialogContent: props for the root layer. className and style go to the root too; ref and every other prop go to the panel, the element with role dialog.

DialogTrigger.description: One child element, a system Button, rendered as the trigger (always asChild). It opens the dialog, gets aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls, and takes focus back on close.

DialogClose.description: One child element, a system Button, that closes the dialog (always asChild). It is marked data-dialog-cancel: in a danger dialog focus opens on it. Wrap only the Cancel action.

data-autofocus.description: Put on any focusable element inside the dialog to take focus on open, before every other rule of the focus rule.

a11y.role: dialog (the panel), modal: Radix hides the rest of the page from assistive tech and keeps focus inside. Named by the title (aria-labelledby), described by the description (aria-describedby).
a11y.focus: On open, focus goes to an element marked data-autofocus; else to the first field in the body; else to the first footer action that is not tone danger; when tone is danger, to the Cancel action (the DialogClose) or else the first footer action that is not tone danger, never a destructive one; else to the close control. On close, focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus before the dialog opened.

keys.Escape: Closes the dialog, unless dismissible is false. Escape from inside the dialog closes the dialog even while a toast shows above it. A nested dialog or a menu on top closes first.
keys.Tab: Moves to the next control inside the dialog and wraps from the last to the first
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves to the previous control inside the dialog and wraps from the first to the last

a11y.announce: The title and the description are read when the dialog opens. The close control and the Desk lights carry their own labels.
notes: role dialog in every tone. A danger dialog stays a dialog: AlertDialog arrives in wave 1 for actions that cannot be undone.
The page behind does not scroll while the dialog is open (Radix scroll lock); pinch zoom stays on.
A body taller than dialog.height-max scrolls inside, and joins the tab order while it scrolls so the keyboard can scroll it. The title and the footer stay in view.
A click on the backdrop closes the dialog, unless dismissible is false. The close control is the button path for the same action.

Toasts sit above an open dialog (z.toast over z.dialog): they stay visible, their live region is not hidden from screen readers, and a pointer click on a toast action or close button works without closing the dialog. Keyboard focus stays in the dialog: F8 and Tab do not reach the toasts (DECISIONS.md, Components 1). Toasts with an action or the danger tone never time out, so they are still there when the dialog closes.
A dialog opened from a dialog stacks above it; Escape closes the top one first and focus returns to its trigger in the first.
The long title wraps, never cut: it is the question being asked.
No native title attribute.

In Desk the title and the close control sit inside the title bar, so they are parts of TitleBar and WindowControls there (a part belongs to the nearest root). The dialog's own parts in Desk are titlebar, description, body and footer; title, close and controls are listed here for Studio and for style.json optionalParts.

dismissible false is for short waits, while the dialog's own action runs. The app must set it back to true when the action ends, success or failure. The close control (the Studio IconButton or the Desk close light) is aria-disabled and stays focusable.
Development builds warn in the console when a dialog opens with no title, and when its footer holds more than three actions.

en.title: The question being asked, in sentence case: Delete the project Spring launch? A task title is fine for a form: Create a board.
en.description: One sentence that says what happens: Its 12 boards go to the trash for 30 days.
en.buttons: Verb plus noun: Delete project, Keep project. Never OK, Yes, Continue or Confirm. Cancel first, the primary action last.

ar.title: The question in white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: تبي تحذف المشروع؟
ar.buttons: Noun form labels, no diacritics: حذف المشروع، إبقاء المشروع. Never نعم or موافق.

react.note: The portal is a Theme that copies the axes of the Theme the Dialog is in (the Toaster pattern), so tokens, language and direction apply inside it.

angular.note: Directives dsDialog (on an ng-container), dsDialogTrigger, dsDialogContent (an ng-template), dsDialogClose, dsDialogBody, dsDialogFooter, dsDialogTitle, dsDialogDescription. The layer renders through a CDK ComponentPortal straight into body, so the DOM equals React's: no cdk-dialog-container and no overlay pane. The portal theme copies every axis of the opening dsTheme. Focus trap on the CDK InteractivityChecker; exit waits for getAnimations. The panel also carries aria-modal. Dialog.css is used as is.

native.note: Renders as a sheet on phones

styles.studio: A flat panel: the solid surface, the panel radius, the dialog shadow. The title sits in a band on surface-2 with a line under it and the close IconButton (part close) at its inline end; the footer is a band on surface-2 with a line over it. The backdrop is the scrim with a light blur. The panel rises 4px and scales up from 98% on duration.base.
styles.desk: Renders as a window with traffic lights: glass with a 24px blur, radius 1rem, a hairline inside, the deep window shadow. The title bar (optional part titlebar) starts with the lights (optional part controls): only the close light works, minimize and zoom are idle and out of the tab order, and the close light is part close. The title sits in the bar and wraps when long. The window grows from 92% on the window open timing. In right to left layouts the lights stay at the top left and the title is centered.

mistakes.wrong: A dialog that only says Saved
mistakes.right: A toast

mistakes.wrong: Buttons that say OK and Cancel
mistakes.right: Verb plus noun: Delete project and Keep project

mistakes.wrong: Focus on the destructive button of a danger dialog
mistakes.right: tone danger and the Cancel action in DialogClose: focus opens on it

mistakes.wrong: A DialogTitle wrapped in a div inside the body
mistakes.right: DialogTitle as a direct child of DialogContent, or the title prop, so it renders once at the top and in the Desk title bar

mistakes.wrong: Hiding the close button in Desk with CSS
mistakes.right: The style turns the titlebar and controls parts on in style.json; Dialog then renders the close light instead of the IconButton

mistakes.wrong: A dialog that closes while its action is still saving
mistakes.right: dismissible false and the primary Button loading until the action ends

mistakes.wrong: Waiting for animationend before removing a closed dialog
mistakes.right: Dialog.css sets the animations to none under reduced motion, so Radix removes the dialog at once

name: Field
summary: Wires one label, one description and one error message to one form control, and passes the invalid, disabled, read only and required state to it.
useWhen: Any form control that needs a visible label
A control with a hint that helps fill it, or an error that says how to fix the value
A settings row with the label at the start and the control at the end (orientation horizontal)
avoidWhen: A search box in a toolbar whose purpose is plain from an icon and an aria-label
A group of checkboxes or radios that shares one question
Read only text that is not a control

orientation.description: vertical: label above the control. horizontal: label at the start of the control's line.

invalid.description: Marks the control invalid. When not passed, the field is invalid while an error message shows. false hides the error.

readOnly.description: Passed to the control. Still focusable and readable.

required.description: Shows the required mark and sets aria-required on the control.

a11y.role: none on the root. The label is a native label bound to the control with for and id.
a11y.focus: The root is never focusable. Clicking the label focuses the control.

keys.Tab: Moves to the control. The field adds no stop of its own.

a11y.announce: The description, then the error, are read with the control through aria-describedby when focus lands there. The error is not a live region and never role alert, so an error that is there when the page loads does not interrupt.
notes: The required mark is an asterisk glyph, so it does not rely on color, and it is aria-hidden. The control carries aria-required, not the native required attribute, so the browser shows no validation bubble.
The error starts with a danger icon, so it does not rely on color.
Controls read the wiring with useFieldControl(): id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, aria-required, disabled and readOnly. A value the control passes itself wins.
A form that checks on submit moves focus to the first invalid control.
Validate on blur or on submit, never on every key. On submit, move focus to the first invalid control.

en.label: A noun in sentence case that names the value: Email, Board name. No colon, no question.
en.description: One sentence that helps fill the field or says where the value shows. Not a repeat of the label.
en.error: Says what to do, in plain words: Add the part after the @. Never only Invalid or Required.
en.placeholder: Never the label. An example value at most: For example, spring launch.
en.required: Mark required fields with * and say once, above the form, that fields marked * are required.

ar.label: اسم بصيغة المصدر أو الاسم، بدون تشكيل: البريد الإلكتروني، اسم اللوحة
ar.description: جملة وحدة توضح وش يكتب أو وين تظهر القيمة
ar.error: يقول وش يسوي عشان يصلحها: البريد ناقص، اكتبه كامل. مو بس غلط
ar.placeholder: ما يكون بديل عن العنوان. مثال على القيمة بس
ar.latin: النص اللاتيني داخل العربي يمر عبر Bidi
ar.required: سطر واحد فوق النموذج: الحقول اللي عليها * مطلوبة

styles.studio: Semibold label, muted description, danger text error with an icon

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder used as the label
mistakes.right: A FieldLabel above the control, and an example value in the placeholder at most

mistakes.wrong: An error that only says Invalid email
mistakes.right: An error that says how to fix it: Add the part after the @, for example name@example.com

mistakes.wrong: role alert on an inline error that is there when the page loads
mistakes.right: FieldError, read through aria-describedby when focus lands on the control

mistakes.wrong: A red asterisk as the only sign of a required field
mistakes.right: required on Field: an aria-hidden asterisk glyph plus aria-required on the control

mistakes.wrong: A label with an id written by hand and a control with a different id
mistakes.right: Field gives both ids. A control id of its own is picked up by the label.

name: Grid
summary: Lays out children in columns and rows: a fixed column count, or as many columns as fit at a minimum item size.
useWhen: Cards, files or tiles of the same kind that line up in columns and rows
A form or settings page with two or three columns on wide screens and one on phones
A twelve column page layout where some cells span more columns
avoidWhen: Items in one line or one column only
Tiles of deliberately mixed sizes on an overview or landing section
Tabular data a person compares across rows
A visual order that differs from the reading order

columns.description: A number from 1 to 12 gives equal tracks. auto-fit fits as many columns as minItemSize allows and grows them to fill the row. Fixed counts fall to one column under breakpoint.phone unless keepColumns is set. Sets data-columns.

minItemSize.description: The smallest item width with auto-fit: sm 10rem, md 15rem, lg 24rem, derived from the breakpoint tokens until a size.grid scale exists. Capped at 100% of the grid, so one item never overflows at 320px. Sets data-min.

gap.description: Space between cells on both axes, a space.* step.

rowGap.description: Space between rows when it differs from gap.

keepColumns.description: Keeps a fixed column count on phones. Sets data-keep-columns. Only for short cells, such as a calendar or a keypad.

as.description: The element to render. ul and ol get role list and lose their bullets; use GridItem as li inside.

GridItem.span.description: Columns the item spans; full spans the whole row. Sets data-span. On phones every item fills the one column.

GridItem.rowSpan.description: Rows the item spans. Sets data-row-span.

GridItem.as.description: The element of the item. li inside a list Grid.

children.description: The cells, plain elements or GridItem.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div, or list on ul and ol
a11y.focus: Never focusable. Focus and reading order are the DOM order: cells fill from the start side, the right in Arabic.
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Grid is layout only.
notes: This is a layout grid, not role grid. A grid of interactive cells with arrow key navigation is a different component (DataGrid).
No dense packing and no order property: the visual order must match the DOM order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
One column under breakpoint.phone and capped track minimums keep the page free of sideways scroll at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10).

en.items: No copy of its own. Cells carry their own labels.

ar.items: No copy of its own. Cells fill from the right in Arabic because the tracks follow dir.

react.note: No motion: a static layout has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies. The phone fallback is a viewport media query; a Grid in a narrow sidebar on a wide screen keeps its columns, so use auto-fit there.

angular.note: The host element is the root and the item, so as is not needed.

native.note: No CSS grid in React Native: fixed columns map to a percentage basis per item and auto-fit to a basis from onLayout width.

styles.studio: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.desk: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.neutral: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.liquid: Layout only. The gap follows density.

mistakes.wrong: columns 4 with fixed pixel widths on each cell
mistakes.right: columns 4, or auto-fit with minItemSize, so tracks shrink and fall to one column on phones

mistakes.wrong: A GridItem span larger than an auto-fit grid has tracks
mistakes.right: span full, or a fixed column count, since auto-fit has fewer tracks on narrow screens

mistakes.wrong: keepColumns on a grid of cards with text
mistakes.right: Leave the phone fallback on; keepColumns is for short cells like a keypad

mistakes.wrong: role grid on a layout Grid
mistakes.right: No role; arrow key navigation between cells belongs to DataGrid

name: Icon
summary: One system icon drawn from the icon set of the active style, sized by the size.icon tokens.
useWhen: A glyph next to a label in a control, a menu item or a status line
An icon only control, where the control carries the accessible name
A status glyph that a label beside it already explains
avoidWhen: An icon that is the only way to tell a meaning and has no label
A brand logo or an illustration
A glyph drawn from a file outside the system names

name.description: A system icon name. Directional names say forward and back.

size.description: 12, 16 and 24 px. The numbers are accepted too.

set.description: An icon set id, pixel or line. Overrides the set of the active style.

label.description: Gives the icon role img and this accessible name. Without it the icon is hidden.

a11y.role: img when label is set, otherwise hidden with aria-hidden
notes: Icons are decoration by default. The control around them carries the name.
Names in the mirror list flip in right to left layouts. Brand marks, clocks and media controls never flip.

angular.note: Generated by packages/icons/build.ts into packages/icons/src/angular. The host svg is the root, glyph nodes come from the Renderer (no innerHTML), the style's icon set comes from dsTheme through the DS_ICON_STYLE signal. Used by dsButton and dsIconButton. No Angular demo yet, so the contract suite does not cover it on its own.

native.note: react-native-svg Icon is generated by packages/icons/build.ts and waits in generated-pending until React Native is installed.

mistakes.wrong: An icon named chevron-right that points the wrong way in Arabic
mistakes.right: chevron-forward, which flips in right to left layouts

mistakes.wrong: An icon only button with the label on the icon
mistakes.right: An IconButton with its own label and a hidden icon

name: IconButton
summary: A square action button with only an icon. Its label is the accessible name and the text of its Tooltip.
useWhen: A toolbar, a header or a row where the icon is well known: close, more, settings
A repeated action in a list where a text label would crowd the row
A close control in a dialog, a panel or a toast
avoidWhen: The icon alone does not say what happens
The main action of a form or a dialog
A choice that stays on or off

insteadUse.The main action of a view: Button with tone accent and emphasis solid

icon.description: A system icon name or a node. Hidden from assistive tech. 16px at every size, lg included, as in both sources.

label.description: The accessible name, set as aria-label. A verb plus a noun. Never the native title attribute. The Tooltip pairing that shows it on hover arrives with Tooltip in wave 1.

size.description: A square of size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px. Never under 24 by 24.

emphasis.description: ghost, because icon buttons sit in toolbars and headers. No link: an icon only link reads as neither.

shape.description: pill is a circle, square takes radius.sm, default takes radius.control (a circle in Desk).

loading.description: The spinner replaces the icon, a visually hidden status says loadingLabel, aria-busy is set, activation is blocked, focus stays.

loadingLabel.description: What the hidden status says while loading.

disabled.description: aria-disabled and data-disabled. Stays focusable so a Tooltip can say why.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example an empty link, as the button.

a11y.role: button (native button element), or the role of the asChild element
a11y.focus: In the tab order in every state. A 2px ring on keyboard focus; solid fills get the doubled ring.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label prop is the accessible name. While loading, a visually hidden status says loadingLabel and aria-busy is set.
notes: label is required by the type, so an icon button always has a name.
At least 24 by 24 CSS px at xs (WCAG 2.5.8). Use lg (44px) in touch layouts.
No native title attribute. The Tooltip pairing that shows the label on hover and focus arrives with Tooltip in wave 1.
Directional icons (chevron-back, arrow-forward) mirror in right to left layouts.
A disabled asChild link loses its href and keeps role link.

en.label: A verb plus a noun in sentence case: Close panel, Open settings. Not the icon name.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: إغلاق اللوحة، فتح الإعدادات.

react.note: Motion: press, named from the pattern catalog that arrives in wave 1. Today: instant color swaps, the spinner, and the Desk roll label.

angular.note: Built on the same base directive as dsButton. label is required and becomes aria-label. Button.css and IconButton.css are used as is.

native.note: Built on the Button internals and Button.styles.ts. label becomes accessibilityLabel and is required. hitSlop reaches 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android at every size. Directional icons mirror from the theme dir. No asChild yet.

styles.studio: Ghost by default, the control radius, the overlay steps on hover and press.
styles.desk: A circle by default (Desk controls are pills). The solid accent icon button is yellow with a doubled focus ring, accent soft a yellow tint. No roll: there is no label.

mistakes.wrong: An icon button with no label, or the label in a title attribute
mistakes.right: label set; the hint in a Tooltip

mistakes.wrong: label="trash"
mistakes.right: label="Delete file"

mistakes.wrong: A 16px icon button in a dense row
mistakes.right: size xs, which keeps the 24px target

mistakes.wrong: A Button with only an icon child
mistakes.right: IconButton

name: Input
summary: A single line text input: a native input in a bordered box with optional start and end adornments.
useWhen: A short value typed on one line: a name, an email, a link, a number
A search box, with the search icon at the start
A value with a unit or a currency shown inside the box
avoidWhen: Text longer than one line
A choice from a known list
A date, a color or a file

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px at default density.

shape.description: default takes radius.control from the style, a pill in Studio and Desk. pill is always fully round.

invalid.description: Marks the value invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: Still focusable, selectable and readable. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

required.description: Sets aria-required. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

start.description: An icon name, a short text such as $, or a node. Icon names and texts are aria-hidden.

end.description: An icon name, a short text such as px, or a node. Icon names and texts are aria-hidden.

rootProps.description: Props for the root box. className and style also go to the root; every other native prop and the ref go to the input.

a11y.role: textbox, from the native input (spinbutton for type number, searchbox for type search)
a11y.focus: The input is the only tab stop. Clicking anywhere in the box that is not interactive focuses the input. Focus shows the glow and a 2px ring around the box.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the input, and on to the next control
keys.Home, End: Move the caret to the start or the end of the value
keys.ArrowUp, ArrowDown: Change the value for type number
keys.Escape: Clears the value for type search, as the browser does

a11y.announce: Name from the Field label. The Field description and error through aria-describedby. aria-invalid and aria-required from the Field.
notes: No native title attribute. Use Tooltip for a hint, or the Field description.
dir auto is not set: the value follows the page direction, so a field does not jump sides while someone types a Latin word into Arabic. Pass dir auto yourself for free text in a mixed language form.
Email, url, tel and number values always run left to right, and stay on the reading side of the form. Their placeholder runs in the page direction.
A long value scrolls inside the box. It is never cut with an ellipsis.
Read only looks different from disabled: a dashed border and a quiet fill, full contrast text, and it stays focusable.
Validate on blur or on submit, never on every key. On submit, move focus to the first invalid control.
Disabled uses native disabled and draws with opacity.disabled, like every control.
A value being checked shows the loader icon in the end slot for now. A Spinner arrives in wave 1 and replaces it.

en.label: Always a visible Field label, a noun in sentence case. aria-label only for a toolbar search box.
en.placeholder: An example value at most: For example, spring launch. Never the label, never an instruction the person needs after typing.
en.adornment: A unit or a currency the value is in: px, USD. Never words the label needs. No icon that only decorates, such as a paper plane on an email field.

ar.label: عنوان ظاهر دايم، بصيغة الاسم وبدون تشكيل
ar.placeholder: مثال على القيمة بس، مو بديل عن العنوان
ar.latin: البريد والروابط والأرقام تنكتب من اليسار لليمين حتى داخل العربي

styles.studio: Bordered transparent pill, the control border, a soft inner glow and the 2px achromatic ring on focus
styles.desk: The same pill and glow, in Instrument Sans

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder as the only label
mistakes.right: A Field with a FieldLabel

mistakes.wrong: An input with a title attribute for the hint
mistakes.right: A FieldDescription, or a Tooltip

mistakes.wrong: A disabled input to show a value that cannot change
mistakes.right: readOnly, which stays readable and focusable

mistakes.wrong: dir auto on every input in an Arabic form
mistakes.right: No dir: email, url, tel and number run left to right through the CSS

mistakes.wrong: type date or checkbox on Input
mistakes.right: The DatePicker or Checkbox component

name: Stack
summary: Lays out children in one direction, a column or a row, with a gap from the space token scale.
useWhen: Children that sit one under the other with an even gap: form fields, cards in a column, a settings list
A row of controls or chips along the line, wrapping when it runs out of room
Pushing two groups to opposite ends of a row with justify between
avoidWhen: Items that must line up in columns and rows at the same time
Centering a page or capping its width
A gap that must be a pixel number outside the space scale
Space added only to separate two groups with a visible line

direction.description: block runs top to bottom (a column). inline runs along the line from the start side (a row), so it starts on the right in Arabic. Sets data-orientation vertical or horizontal.

gap.description: A space.* step. Fluid, and follows the density axis. Never a number.

align.description: Cross axis alignment (align-items). Logical words only: start is the right edge in a right to left row.

wrap.description: Lets children wrap onto more lines. Sets data-wrap.

as.description: The element to render. ul and ol lose their bullets and get role list, so Safari keeps the list semantics.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element as the Stack through Radix Slot. Wins over as. A ul or ol child loses its bullets, so give it role list yourself.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div by default, the semantics of as or the asChild element otherwise; list on ul and ol
a11y.focus: Never focusable. Focus order is DOM order, which is also the visual order: no reverse directions.
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Stack is layout only.
notes: There is no row-reverse or column-reverse. Reversing the visual order would break the reading and focus order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
Inline direction follows dir: the first child sits on the right in Arabic with no extra prop.

en.items: No copy of its own. Children carry their own labels.

ar.items: No copy of its own. The row starts on the right in Arabic because the words are logical.

react.behavior: hand built flex box, radix:Slot for asChild
react.note: No motion: a static layout has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies.

angular.note: The host element is the root, so as and asChild are not needed: put the directive on a ul, nav or section.

native.note: direction inline maps to row, which I18nManager flips in right to left. Gap from the generated space values.

styles.studio: Layout only. The gap scale follows density.
styles.desk: Layout only. The gap scale follows density.
styles.neutral: Layout only. The gap scale follows density.
styles.liquid: Layout only. The gap scale follows density.

mistakes.wrong: direction row with a margin-left on each child
mistakes.right: direction inline with a gap step, which works in both reading directions

mistakes.wrong: A gap of 12 as a number
mistakes.right: gap l (12px in the default density on a wide screen), a space step that follows density

mistakes.wrong: A Stack used to make a two dimension card grid with nested rows
mistakes.right: Grid with columns or auto-fit

mistakes.wrong: Reversing the order with CSS so the last child shows first
mistakes.right: Change the order in the markup, so reading and focus order match

name: Theme
summary: Stamps every runtime axis on its own element, resolves what is not passed from the nearest parent Theme, and gives the subtree its direction, icon set and style data.
useWhen: At the root of an app, once, so tokens, base CSS, direction and icons apply
Around a subtree that needs another scheme, style, density, language or direction
Around a demo or a preview that shows one combination of axes
avoidWhen: Changing one color or size in one place: use a component prop or a token
Setting dir or lang alone on an element: the tokens, Radix and the icons would not follow
Wrapping every component: one Theme per subtree that changes an axis is enough

style.description: The style pack id. Any custom id is accepted. At the root the default is studio; nested, the parent's.

scheme.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested. A scheme the style does not list falls back to its default.

density.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested.

glass.description: Read only by styles that use glass.

dir.description: Follows lang when lang is passed and dir is not. Otherwise the parent's, then from lang.

lang.description: A BCP 47 tag. The system ships en and ar.

css.description: Inline styles for the Theme element, as a React style object. style is taken by the style axis.

a11y.focus: Never focusable. It adds no role.
notes: dir and lang on the element let screen readers pick the right voice and let CSS mirror the layout.
The Radix direction provider follows dir, so menus, sliders and arrow keys mirror in right to left.
Arabic text gets IBM Plex Sans Arabic, zero tracking, taller lines and small text one step up through base.css. Body text keeps its size.

en.lang: Set lang on the root Theme. A Latin island inside Arabic is any element with lang en; it gets the Latin type back.

ar.lang: Set lang ar on the root Theme. dir follows as rtl.

react.note: Exports Theme, useTheme, useOptionalPart, themeAttributes and resolveTheme from packages/react/src/theme.

angular.note: dsTheme directive in packages/angular/src/theme, inputs named like the React props. A static style="desk" never reaches the style input (the Angular compiler parses it as inline CSS): bind [style]="'desk'" or use dsTheme="desk". Inline styles pass through css. Provides DsThemeService (value signal, optionalPart), the CDK Directionality and the icon style to its subtree. applyDocumentTheme stamps the html element.

native.note: ThemeProvider passes the resolved theme object through context, with the same axis names.

styles.studio: Black body, Inter Variable, default density
styles.desk: Black desk, Instrument Sans, default density, window and dialog controls and titlebar turned on

mistakes.wrong: <div dir="rtl" lang="ar"> around a screen
mistakes.right: <Theme lang="ar">, which also sets dir, the Radix direction and the Arabic type

mistakes.wrong: <Theme style={{ padding: 8 }}>
mistakes.right: <Theme css={{ padding: 8 }}>: style is the style axis

mistakes.wrong: Reading data-style from the DOM to pick a branch
mistakes.right: useTheme().style, or useOptionalPart for a part only one style shows

name: TitleBar
summary: The bar at the top of a window or a panel: window controls at the start, the title, then trailing actions.
useWhen: The header of a Window, or of a Dialog drawn as a window in Desk
A panel header that needs a title and a close button
avoidWhen: The header of a page
A toolbar of many tools with no title

title.description: The title. One line with an ellipsis.

titleId.description: id of the title, for aria-labelledby on the window or dialog.

actions.description: The end slot: IconButtons and small Buttons.

moveLabel.description: Puts the title in a focusable move handle (part move, role group) named by this label: "Move window". The host (Window) listens for the keys there.

moveHint.default: Arrow keys move the window. Shift moves it further.
moveHint.description: Description of the move handle, through aria-describedby.

a11y.role: none: a plain container. The title is a heading (h2 by default).
a11y.focus: The bar itself is not focusable. With moveLabel the move handle is a tab stop with the 2px ring; while it has keyboard focus the title wraps to show in full. Then the controls and actions take focus in order.

keys.Tab: Moves through the controls, the move handle and the actions

a11y.announce: The heading is read in document order. A window or dialog points aria-labelledby at titleId.
notes: The title truncates with an ellipsis; the full text stays in the DOM, and keyboard focus on the move handle shows it wrapped.
Parts minimize, zoom and close are IconButtons a host renders in the actions slot when it has no lights (Window in Studio). They belong to the TitleBar, their nearest root.
In right to left layouts a bar with controls keeps them at the top left and centers the title, as macOS draws it. A bar without controls mirrors.

en.title: A file or app name in sentence case.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics. Latin file names go through Bidi.

angular.note: A first port exists for the Desk dialog chrome (packages/angular/src/components/title-bar): controls, title (a string, a TemplateRef or an ng-template dsTitleBarTitle), actions, as, titleId, active, with the React DOM. No move handle and no demo yet; it turns ready with Window. TitleBar.css is used as is.

native.note: Native screens use the platform navigation bar.

styles.studio: A plain header on the panel surface with a hairline under it (recipes/Window.css when inside a Window).
styles.desk: Transparent, as the source .dwin-bar: the window glass shows through, no divider. The lights sit at the start.

mistakes.wrong: A title in a native title attribute to show the full text
mistakes.right: The full text stays in the title; a Tooltip shows it

mistakes.wrong: Mirroring the lights in Arabic
mistakes.right: The lights keep their place and order; only a bar without lights mirrors

name: Toast
summary: A short notice that something happened, shown in a corner and gone on its own. Called from anywhere with toast(); one Toaster renders them.
useWhen: Confirming that an action the person took has finished: Draft saved, Link copied
A failure the person can fix later or retry from the toast, as tone danger with one action
A background event worth knowing now: a new version, a finished upload
Progress that ends in a result, updated in place with toast.update
avoidWhen: The person needs to make a decision before going on
Long content, a list, or anything to read twice
A critical error that blocks the task or loses data
A message tied to one field or one place on the page
Something that must stay on screen while the condition lasts

parts.Toast: root, without behavior and without data-state
parts.isInsideToaster: helper for overlays: true for a target inside the toaster

tone.description: The color and icon, and the timing: neutral, info and success close after 4s, warning after 6s, danger stays until closed.

title.description: One line: what happened, naming the thing.

description.description: More detail. Long text wraps in full; keep it to one or two sentences.

duration.description: toast() option. Milliseconds before it closes; Infinity keeps it. Default by tone. Ignored for danger and for a toast with an action, which stay until closed. toast.configure({ durations, max }) lengthens them for the whole app.

action.description: toast() option. One button: { label, onAction, altText }. A toast with an action never times out. altText is read in place of the button, for example where else the same action lives.

dedupeKey.description: toast() option. A toast that reads the same as an open one bumps its count instead of stacking; a key groups repeats with other copy; false turns it off.

id.description: toast() option. A call with the id of an open toast updates it.

lang.description: toast() option. The language of the copy when it differs from the page. The root gets lang and dir.

count.description: Toast prop. The repeat count; the Toaster passes it from the store.

onClose.description: Toast prop. Renders the close button and is called by it. The Toaster always renders it.

closeLabel.description: The accessible name of the close button. Arabic under lang ar.

position.description: Toaster prop. end is the inline end: right in English, left in Arabic.

label.description: Toaster prop. The name of the region. {hotkey} in it is replaced by the hotkey.

hotkey.description: Toaster prop. The keys that move focus to the toasts.

store.description: Toaster prop. The store to render. Default the app wide store behind toast().

a11y.role: The Toaster is a region (named Notifications) holding a list; each toast is a list item. Announcements go through two visually hidden regions owned by the Toaster: role status (polite) and role alert (assertive, for danger).
a11y.focus: Not modal: toasts never take focus on their own. F8 moves focus to the list, which shows the focus ring; Tab moves through the toasts, newest first, and each toast's action and close button. Closing the focused toast puts focus on the list. While a dialog with a focus trap is open, keyboard focus stays in the dialog: the toasts stay visible, readable and clickable, and a toast with an action waits until the dialog closes.

keys.F8: Moves focus to the notifications list
keys.Tab: Moves to the next toast, action or close button
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action or close button
keys.Escape: Closes a toast only when the key comes from inside the toaster: the focused toast, or the newest one from the list. Escape anywhere else, in a Window, a Dialog or a form, leaves every toast alone, a danger toast included, and is not prevented, so the system Dialog still closes itself. A raw Radix Dialog from a consumer does not get that Escape while a toast shows above it (Radix gives Escape to the top layer only), so use the system Dialog or close the toast first.

a11y.announce: Once per change (WCAG 4.1.3): when a toast shows, and again on each repeat or update, as "Notification. Title. Description. Action alternative." with the toast's text in the toast's language. danger is assertive (role alert), the rest polite (role status). The toast itself has no live role and keeps its element across a repeat or update, so it is never read twice and focus stays. Radix's own announcer is muted. The close button is not read.
notes: danger toasts and toasts with an action stay until closed. The others pause while the pointer is over them, while focus is inside, and while the window is blurred or the tab hidden (WCAG 2.2.1). toast.configure({ durations }) lengthens them for the whole app.
Swipe toward the edge closes a toast; the close button is the button path for the same action (WCAG 2.5.7).

Above an open modal dialog the toasts stay visible (z.toast is above z.dialog), stay in the accessibility tree and take the pointer. A dialog calls isInsideToaster(event.target) in onFocusOutside, onPointerDownOutside and onInteractOutside and prevents the default, so a toast never closes it.
At most three toasts show at once; the rest wait their turn, so a burst never covers the page.
No native title attribute anywhere.

en.title: Say what happened and name the thing: Draft saved, Could not upload photo.jpg. Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
en.description: Optional. What it means or what to do next, in one or two short sentences. Long text wraps in full, so keep it short.
en.action: A verb plus a noun: Retry upload, Undo move, Open draft. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes. One action at most. The toast then stays until closed.
en.danger: Name the failure and what is safe: Could not publish page. Your draft is safe.
en.repeats: Keep the copy the same for the same event, so repeats fold into one toast with a count.

ar.title: Say what happened and name the thing, in noun forms where you can: المسودة محفوظة، تعذر رفع الصورة. No diacritics.
ar.action: Noun form labels, no diacritics: إعادة الرفع، تراجع عن النقل. Never the imperative.
ar.digits: Western digits. Latin names in the copy go through Bidi when the toast is rendered by hand.
ar.lang: Pass lang: "ar" when the page is not Arabic, so the toast gets the Arabic type and direction.

react.note: Toaster renders the shared store from @the-system/shared; toast is re-exported from @the-system/react.

angular.behavior: the shared toast store with cdk:a11y LiveAnnouncer
angular.note: Reuses the store, its timers and Toast.css as is; reports pause and resume like the React Toaster.

native.note: The same store. Safe areas and reduce motion from the platform.

styles.studio: A flat surface card with a hairline border and a 2px edge in the tone color on the inline start side.
styles.desk: Glass notifications as on the desk: strong glass fill, window blur, window radius and the soft window shadow (recipes/Toast.css). Solid under reduced transparency and more contrast.
styles.neutral: Planned: a white card with a small shadow.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass capsule at the top center.

mistakes.wrong: A toast for an error that blocks the task, such as a lost session
mistakes.right: An AlertDialog that says what happened and how to go on

mistakes.wrong: A danger toast that closes itself after a few seconds
mistakes.right: danger stays until closed; the store ignores a duration for it

mistakes.wrong: A toast with two buttons, or an action labelled OK
mistakes.right: One action at most, a verb plus a noun: Retry upload

mistakes.wrong: The same toast stacked five times by a retry loop
mistakes.right: Same copy, one toast with a count. Dedupe is on by default.

mistakes.wrong: A second Toaster for Arabic copy
mistakes.right: One Toaster per page; pass lang: "ar" on the toast

mistakes.wrong: A toast as the only place a result lives
mistakes.right: Show the result on the page too; the toast only says it happened

mistakes.wrong: Mounting the Toaster inside a dialog or outside the root Theme
mistakes.right: Mount it once inside the root Theme, before any dialog can open

mistakes.wrong: A dialog that closes when the person clicks a toast above it
mistakes.right: Call isInsideToaster(event.target) in the dialog's outside handlers and prevent the default

name: Window
summary: An app window over the page: a title bar, a body and an optional footer. It opens from a trigger, moves, zooms, minimizes and closes. Desk draws it as a glass window with traffic lights; Studio as a flat panel with a close button.
useWhen: A tool or a document the person works in next to the page: a board, a file browser, settings
Several views the person arranges side by side and brings to the front
Content that opens from a control and should grow out of it
avoidWhen: A decision that blocks the page until it is made
A short message with no work in it
A list of actions behind one control
Content that belongs in the page flow

kind.description: Sets data-kind. canvas: a large window with a margin of layer around it, no body padding. finder: wide, the layer edge around it. settings: centered, as tall as its content.

title.description: Names the window through aria-labelledby. One line with an ellipsis.

actions.description: IconButtons or small Buttons at the end of the title bar, before the window buttons. They are TitleBar parts.

footer.description: The footer part, for the window's Buttons.

open.description: Controlled open state, with onOpenChange. Closing plays window-close, then unmounts.

zoomed.description: Fills the layer. Sets data-zoomed and aria-pressed on the zoom light.

onZoomedChange.description: With it, or inside a WindowLayer, zoom works: the zoom light (Desk), the zoom IconButton (Studio), Enter on the move handle and a double click on the title bar.

minimized.description: Plays window-minimize toward the dock, then hides the window. Sets data-minimized.

onMinimizedChange.description: With it minimize works: the minimize light (Desk) or IconButton (Studio). The app shows the way back (a dock) and sets minimized to false.

frame.description: { x, y, width, height } in px: x from the inline start edge of the layer, y from the top. null lets the kind place the window. Controlled with onFrameChange.

onFrameChange.description: Called on every move by key or pointer, with the clamped frame.

movable.description: Drag by the title bar and move with the arrow keys. Default true inside a WindowLayer or with a frame, false for a window placed by its parent.

origin.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect the window grows out of and closes back into. Focus returns to it on close.

dock.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect a minimized window falls into. Default the bottom center of the layer. Focus goes to it when nothing before it in the focus order can take focus.

modal.description: aria-modal and a Tab loop inside the window. Off by default: windows sit next to the page.

moveLabel.description: Name of the move handle: the title of a window that can move, focusable, a TitleBar part.

moveHint.description: Description of the move handle. Default names the arrow keys, Shift, and Enter when zoom works.

a11y.role: dialog, named by the title (aria-labelledby) or aria-label. Not modal unless modal is set.
a11y.focus: Focus moves into the window (the window element, tabindex -1) when it opens after mount, or on mount when its origin has focus. When the window closes or minimizes, focus goes to the first of: the origin, the next active window of the layer, the element that had focus before it opened, the dock, the WindowLayer (a region with tabindex -1). It moves only when focus was in the window or lost. Keyboard focus and pointer down both bring a window to the front.

keys.Escape: Closes the window. A control inside that handles Escape itself (a menu) prevents it first.
keys.ArrowUp: Moves the window up 16px, while focus is on the window or on its move handle (the title)
keys.ArrowDown: Moves the window down 16px, from the same places
keys.ArrowLeft: Moves the window 16px to the left on screen, in both directions
keys.ArrowRight: Moves the window 16px to the right on screen, in both directions
keys.Shift+ArrowUp, Shift+ArrowDown, Shift+Ar: Moves the window 64px, from the same places
keys.Enter: On the move handle: zooms the window or puts it back, when zoom works
keys.Tab: Moves through the lights or the title bar buttons, the move handle, the title bar actions, the body and the footer. With modal, Tab stays inside the window.

a11y.announce: The title is the accessible name of the dialog. The lights and the close button carry their own labels.
notes: Every drag has a key path (WCAG 2.1.1, 2.5.7): the arrow keys move the window from the window element or the move handle. The frame is clamped so 160px of the window and its title bar stay inside the layer.
Arrow keys pressed on a light, an action or anything in the body never move the window, so a roving toolbar in actions keeps its arrows.
Zoom has a key and a button in every style: Enter on the move handle, the zoom light in Desk, the zoom IconButton in Studio. A double click on the title bar is a pointer shortcut for the same action.
Moving is off while the window is zoomed, and for a window placed by its parent with no frame. The move handle is rendered only while the window can move.
Tab order follows the DOM order of the windows, not their stacking. Moving focus into a window with Tab brings it to the front.
A long title truncates with an ellipsis; the full text is the accessible name, and keyboard focus on the move handle wraps the title to show it in full.
No native title attribute.

Contract suite: Escape is checked in the many case, where closing the front window makes the next one active (data-state changes). The arrow keys move the frame (inline position), which no contract.keys expectation reads yet, so the suite notes them; Window.test.tsx covers them.

angular.note: Window.css, TitleBar.css and WindowControls.css are used as is.

native.note: Phones and tablets have no free windows. A native app shows the same content as a full screen or a sheet; see Dialog and Drawer.

styles.studio: A flat panel: the solid surface, the panel radius and shadow, no backdrop blur, a hairline under a plain title bar. No lights: minimize, zoom and close are IconButtons at the end of the title bar, minimize and zoom only when the window can do them. Open, close and minimize fade on duration.base; zoom has no motion.
styles.desk: A glass window: material glass with a 24px blur, radius 1rem, a hairline inside, the deep window shadow, a transparent title bar as in the source. The title bar starts with the traffic lights (optional part controls): idle dots at rest, colors and glyphs on hover or keyboard focus of the group. The window grows out of its trigger, closes back into it, zooms with a FLIP and falls into the dock. The layer carries the desk grain. In right to left layouts the lights stay at the top left and the title is centered.

name: WindowControls
summary: The traffic lights of a window: close, minimize and zoom. 12px lights with 24 by 24 px targets, each an IconButton with its own label.
useWhen: The controls slot of a TitleBar in a style that turns the window controls part on (Desk)
A window picture where the lights are shown but do nothing, with no handlers
avoidWhen: A panel in a style without lights (Studio)
Any control that is not close, minimize or zoom of a window

onClose.description: Without it the close light is disabled.

closeDisabled.description: With onClose: the close light is aria-disabled and data-disabled, stays in the tab order, blocks activation and draws as an idle dot; its glyph still shows on hover and focus. For a window or dialog that cannot be dismissed right now.

onMinimize.description: Without it the minimize light is disabled.

onZoom.description: Without it the zoom light is disabled.

active.description: data-state active or inactive, for hosts and recipes. As in the source, it does not change how the lights look.

a11y.role: group, named by label. Each light is a native button (IconButton).
a11y.focus: Each light with a handler is in the tab order with the 2px ring around its 24px target. A light with no handler is aria-disabled and out of the tab order (tabIndex -1): an accepted exception to the rule that disabled actions stay focusable, because a dead light is inert decoration of the window chrome; a screen reader still finds it, dimmed. A close light disabled through closeDisabled is an action that cannot run now: it stays focusable with aria-disabled, like any disabled Button.

keys.Enter: Presses the focused light. Nothing happens on a disabled light.
keys.Tab: Moves to the next light with a handler

a11y.announce: Each light is named by its label. The zoom light reports pressed while the window is zoomed.
notes: Never color alone: the glyphs (x, minus, arrows) show with the colors on hover and on keyboard focus of the group, and always in forced colors.
The lights do not mirror in right to left layouts. They keep the order close, minimize, zoom from the left, as macOS draws them and as the source does.
Targets are 24 by 24 px and touch, so light centers are 24px apart (WCAG 2.5.8).
No native title attribute.

angular.note: A first port exists for the Desk dialog chrome (packages/angular/src/components/window-controls), with the React DOM. The handlers are function inputs named like the React props (onClose, onMinimize, onZoom): a light with no handler is disabled, and an Angular output cannot tell whether anyone listens. No demo yet; it turns ready with Window. WindowControls.css is used as is.

native.note: Native apps have no window lights.

styles.studio: Not drawn inside a Window (the controls part is off). Standalone it draws the same lights.
styles.desk: The traffic lights at the start of every window title bar. As in the source: idle dots at rest, the three colors on hover or focus within the group; this system adds the glyphs in the same state.
